comments.author: Guilder
comments.body:
Those who have played a game longer will always have an advantage over those who have not. Those who invest in keeping a game alive will reap benefits greater than those who do not. This is not an issue of "balance", as much as it is a time-honored rule of MMOs, which are run as a business, not a charity.

The beauty of this game lies not in being the "best" or "strongest" or "richest" player. It's in the voyage of discovery and adventure, of memorable times spent with your fellow voyagers and friends. It's a vastly rewarding and rich experience, where pretty much any method or style of play is valid, except to those few who cry "foul" and try, unnecessarily, to dictate terms of what counts as the "real" way to play.

I know I will never be among the "top dogs" of UWO, and that's fine by me. I'll have fun my own way, gladly saluting those that fund this game I love so, and not begrudging them their fringe benefits, even if I sometimes look at their Astro ships and drool over the them, just a little. I don't have to pay to win anything; I am free to do so if I want an advantage in the game, big or small, but UWO is fully playable without such expenses. Far moreso than most MMOs are, I would add.

More than that, UWO is a wonderful game for those who give it a chance, and who have the right mindset for its unique and distinctive nature. It rewards long-term planning, unorthodox styles of play, and a willingness to not be afraid to try new things.

But if it's not to your liking, then I'm sure you'll find a game out there somewhere that you'll enjoy more. If you choose to give it a little longer, that's fine too. Those of us who come here to the UWO DB for tips, guides, and the sort, would appreciate it if you'd consider using the official forums to discuss matters like these in the future; that's not a demand, only a suggestion, of course.

Cheers, either way. Hope you find a way to have fun, whether here or somewhere else.

comments.author: Guilder
comments.body:
The game continues to grow, and change. Things do not remain static, for better or worse. If you're old enough, you surely recall the original land battle system, compared to its present form? When beginner school didn't exist, how different job changing was? Or how spice goods weren't properly valued while EA goods were overvalued? When you couldn't buy Hanseatic/Miser/RIBs in item shops? When pirates could steal your EQ and ship parts? Those things, and more, have changed. Many more things about UWO will continue to do so as time passes.

Being a business, MMOs do not reward casual play as well as they do single-minded, hours-long devotion spent playing them (and possibly spending real life money on them as well). This is easily seen in any MMO you could think to name; it's the same as in life, really. Those who spend time at a gym and work out, are going to have an advantage versus those who don't.

Likewise, "balance" can never be fully achieved, because everyone has their own ideas on what it should be, and there's no pleasing everybody -- I guarantee if we were all capped at 5/5/5, 50k ducats, and sailing in identically statted barcas, somebody would claim another player's barca was unfairly better than theirs, while somebody else tried to sell their G6 barca for 1m ducats.

As for ESF, I've done fine there. I stick with players who are fun to play with, and reasonably powerful; gotten several court ranks that way. A few times we've even beaten big deal PVPers and their money ships, through solid teamwork and good tactics. That always feels good; more than I think it would if we were identically powerful, though perhaps that's just me.

I didn't know trade could be competitive; thought it was just about selling for a profit, and gaining levels until they're maxed? I must just be ignorant that way, since it's not a field I care all that much about. I didn't know adventure was "unbalanced", either. Seems to still be the hardest thing to level in the game, though certainly (for me at least) the most rewarding and fun. And dungeons? They're just a different way to play the game. 2nd Age and Gran Atlas reduced their ticket-running profit potential a great deal, so I don't see anything unbalanced there.

Bottomline: Gaps in strength and wealth will always exist; fixes will likewise always surface here and there to try to level the field some, but no game will ever be 100% "perfect" in that regard.

Well, Im not going to favour anyone in this conversation because both of you are right to some degree.

There are few real players out there, most of other "new players" are alts belonging to the oldest players.

I had a old friend, she owned several cash ships and her own fully depeloped company plus being a r20 sb plus other skills, she quit the game arguin same stuff that Lexy guys is speaking off. As a some kind of memento, she gave me a cash ship and some cash items to improve it; I'm a casual too and I observed how a ship, even if it is no cash ship, gets better with SSIP (done correctly) even if you dont use expensive cash FS parts. The game is still playable and fun to play even if you don't spend a single penny in it but it limits you gameplay a lot.

Every body can purchase astro ships or older nc ships with in-game currency, same goes for fs parts.

There are resellers whom like to exchange real money for virtual money and fake ships, maybe that is stupid but for some people that is cool because that is an opportunity for non money spenders to get a powerfull cash ship. The negative thing is the time it will takes to get the INSANE amount of ducats for those ships, is HUGE; come on? 32B for a ship? Come on!! It' will take me like a whole year to get that amount if I play 4-6 hours a day, and that is just for the ship... I need to pay for SSIPs, the item for the dismantle the ship, cash FS parts, and shipbuilder wages. All of that is way easier if you have money, you purchase most of those items within reach of a button, just a click away from you credit card, pay pal o your wallet.

Game is pretty nice, good graphics without being too demanding, very balanced and well developed game mechanics but it seems it favour money spenders, game policy is againt selling ships directly to avoid making a obvious pay2win but it already is, a discrete p2w. You can purchase ships directly within montly champion pack, you gamble on sailos bottle for a chance to get an astro ship, isn't that paying to get more power, to get advantage over other players? A game could be profitable and non p2w at the same time, there is a lot of those games out there.

Anyway, I'm going to keep playing, I enjoy it, it's a very nice game.
